experiments.scope: Reduced event on the selected Orchard Poseidon target at its own round count: the first 14 bits of the big-endian reading of the 32-byte digest agree for two distinct canonical messages. One birthday search per organizer trial over fresh inputs from the trial seed. No full collision is expected or claimed.
experiments.hypothesis: A search of at most 1200 fresh inputs returns a pair whose digests agree on those 14 bits in every trial. The count of trials that return a pair is a reproducible observation; no probability, rate or population bound is drawn from it (public organizer seeds; nothing is assumed about the seeded trials being independent or identically distributed). Checks the digest of the selected target at one reduced width; it says nothing about the full-width map, the cost or the success probability.

experiments.scope: One trial of the algorithm at reduced depth, on the selected Orchard Poseidon target (proof.md 9.1, 10.5.1). For a centre c from the trial seed the program builds F_2(c + X) (the F_N of proof.md 10.3, degree 25), its monic odd part g (degree m = 12), R = X^((p-1)/2) mod g and the complete Euclidean sequence of (g, R - 1) with its gcd G, exactly over F_p; deg G = k(c), the number of usable roots. If the sequence is normal and 1 <= k(c) <= 16, it isolates a root S of G (stage E, shifts from the seed), takes s = sqrt(S) and checks F_2(c + s) = F_2(c - s) by direct evaluation. Trials 0-255 are computed. A trial that passes returns two distinct canonical messages on the line whose digests agree on the first 6 bits (65 line points, certain by pigeonhole); any other trial returns two nulls. The checked pair count is the number of centres where one trial at depth 2 succeeds. The Graeffe prefix of proof.md 4.3G is off in this test (s = 0: R = X^((p-1)/2) mod g and s = sqrt(S)); it tests H-ONE, a statement about g that the prefix does not change.
experiments.hypothesis: Every computed sequence is normal (H-NORMAL), and a trial returns a pair exactly when 1 <= k(c) <= 16 and its isolated root passes the check; at m = 12 the fraction of centres with 1 <= k(c) <= 16 is given by the law of proof.md 9.3, a theorem at this depth. The pair count is a reproducible observation consistent with that law; no probability, rate or population bound is drawn from it (public organizer seeds; nothing is assumed about the seeded trials being independent or identically distributed). Per computed trial the program reports the untrusted observations n_layers, m, gcd_degree, normal, abnormal_quotients, selfcheck, iso_rounds, root_check and witness_points. A trial is counted only when its sequence is also normal, which only lowers the count (a normal sequence down to the gcd is what lets the root be isolated and verified). Supports the premise H-ONE at m = 12 on the construction's own polynomial; it says nothing about the scale m = 122,070,312 of the claim, where it is extrapolated.

experiments.scope: Euclidean normality of this construction at reduced depth, on the selected Orchard Poseidon target (proof.md 9.5, 10.5.1). For a centre c from the trial seed the program builds F_2(c + X), the coordinate 0 after the first 2 S-box layers on the line j = 0 of the first two rounds (the F_N of proof.md 10.3, degree 25), its monic odd part about c (degree m = 12), g = the 24-fold Graeffe transform of that odd part (proof.md 4.3G; monic, degree m), R = X^((p-1)/2^25) mod g and the complete Euclidean remainder sequence of (g, R - 1), exactly over F_p. Trials 0-255 are computed. A computed trial whose sequence is normal (deg(R - 1) = m - 1 and every quotient of degree 1 down to the gcd) returns two distinct canonical messages on the line whose digests agree on the first 6 bits, found among 65 line points (certain, by pigeonhole); any other trial returns two nulls. No full collision is expected or claimed.
experiments.hypothesis: Every computed sequence is normal, so exactly 256 of the 256 trials return a pair. Per computed trial the program reports the untrusted observations deg_r_minus_1, steps (m - deg gcd when normal), abnormal_quotients, first_abnormal_step, max_quotient_degree and gcd_degree (positive when k(c) >= 1, a usable root; at m = 12 for c uniform the law of H-ONE (proof.md 9.3) gives P(k(c) >= 1) between 0.39346933 and 0.39346944, a theorem at this depth; no rate is drawn from the seeded trials). Supports the premise H-NORMAL of proof.md 9.5 at m = 12 on the construction's own pairs; it says nothing about the scale m of the claim, the cost or the success probability.

experiments.scope: Euclidean normality of this construction at reduced depth, on the selected Orchard Poseidon target (proof.md 9.5, 10.5.1). Two centres per trial, the first from the trial seed, the second from the seed and its index. For each centre c the program builds F_2(c + X), the coordinate 0 after the first 2 S-box layers on the line j = 0 of the first two rounds (the F_N of proof.md 10.3, degree 25), its monic odd part about c (degree m = 12), g = the 24-fold Graeffe transform of that odd part (proof.md 4.3G; monic, degree m), R = X^((p-1)/2^25) mod g and the complete Euclidean remainder sequence of (g, R - 1), exactly over F_p. All 256 trials are computed, 512 sequences. A trial whose two sequences are both normal (deg(R - 1) = m - 1 and every quotient of degree 1 down to the gcd) and pass the self-checks returns two distinct canonical messages on the line whose digests agree on the first 6 bits, found among 65 line points (certain, by pigeonhole); any other trial returns two nulls. The final letter of the id only changes the organizer seeds. No full collision is expected or claimed.
experiments.hypothesis: Every computed sequence is normal, so exactly 256 of the 256 trials return a pair and the abnormal count is zero in 512 sequences. Per trial the program reports the untrusted observations sequences, normal_sequences, selfcheck_ok, abnormal_quotients, gcd_positive and max_quotient_degree. Zero abnormal sequences in the 3,072 sequences of the six -l2 entries is a reproducible observation consistent with H-NORMAL; no population bound is drawn from it (delta = 0.003 is the declared premise). Supports the premise H-NORMAL of proof.md 9.5 at m = 12 on the construction's own pairs; it says nothing about the scale m of the claim, the cost or the success probability.
